chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I allow the testimony of women regarding the boy, whether he cried or did not cry, and in everything that men do not look at, the testimony of women is allowed regarding it.

key_terms.لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ الرِّجَالُ: that men do not look at

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the scope of female testimony by linking its validity to the domain of visual inspection, ruling that women’s testimony is accepted in matters where men do not typically look, such as verifying a newborn's cry. This principle highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of aligning legal capacity with social and biological realities, ensuring that testimony is sought from those with direct, relevant observation. It serves as a foundational text for understanding gender-specific roles in evidentiary matters within Islamic law.
